topics.topic: Required returned-message behavior when a returned value exceeds the resource limit
questions: Must an oversized returned value still produce the required returned message containing an output for each key, or must it produce only the resource hit and no outputs?

quotes: Before it builds that message it MUST pre-count the representable outputs against output_bytes — each value output as the UTF-8 bytes of that json.dumps, each file as its bytes — and when the pre-count exceeds output_bytes write a resource hit and no outputs; a MemoryError while it pre-counts, encodes or writes the outputs is a resource hit too, so an output too large to send concludes resource_exhausted rather than crashed.
judgement.why: The conditional resource-limit rule explicitly requires a resource hit and no outputs when the pre-count exceeds output_bytes.

topics.topic: Whether judge_execution may use bounds in addition to observation
questions: Must judge_execution decide from observation alone, or may it also use bounds as the output-count rule requires?

quotes: judge_execution: [BEHAVIOR] MUST decide from the observation alone and run nothing.

The output count is the sum of the canonical bytes (from canonical_bytes) of every value output and the bytes of every file output, a many file output counting each element, compared with bounds.output_bytes; it decides whenever the outputs reach the parent, and output over a bound is a failure, never truncated.
judgement.why: The first passage forbids relying on anything beyond observation, while the second requires using bounds.output_bytes, which is supplied separately from observation.

topics.topic: Required reference and naming behavior for RecordedSource flow outputs
questions: Must a RecordedSource return its existing ref unchanged, or must the result always be a StoredValuesRef renamed to the flow output port's name?

quotes: A RecordedSource MUST answer its ref;
Returns the StoredValuesRef named by the flow output port's name.
judgement.why: Returning the existing reference unchanged can preserve a different port name, while the return-shape requirement mandates the flow output port's name.

topics.topic: When a mapped node is considered concluded
questions: Does one skipped_by_guard or upstream_failed element record immediately conclude a mapped node, or must the mapped node remain unconcluded until every element has concluded?

quotes: a skipped_by_guard or upstream_failed record concludes its node so, a function node and an operation node alike — for an operation element through the ElementFailed with that status operation_element_conclusion answers, as said above: skipped_by_guard concludes the node skipped and upstream_failed concludes it upstream_failed;
a mapped node concludes only when every element concluded, succeeded only when all succeeded.
judgement.why: One passage makes a single skipped or upstream-failed element record conclude its mapped node, while the other requires every element to conclude first.

topics.topic: Whether an empty mapped list has zero elements or a synthetic unindexed element
questions: Must an empty mapped list have no elements because elements are list positions, or must it have the specified synthetic element without map_index?

quotes: A mapped node's elements are the positions of the list delivered to its map_over port, counted from the JSON array its StoredValue holds — read with read_value_bytes, or the canonical_json of an AssembledList not yet written — or the files of its SpooledFilesRef;

a mapped node over an empty list is ready with over_empty_list and one element without map_index whose sources are the node's inputs as delivered — its map_over port's source is the source of the empty list itself, a RecordedSource or a MappedListSource, never a ListElementSource, which exists only for an element with a map_index;
judgement.why: An empty list has no positions under the first passage, but the second passage requires one synthetic unindexed element.

topics.topic: Whether flow inputs traverse all outgoing edges or only guard-enabled edges
questions: Are flow inputs delivered along every outgoing edge, or only along outgoing edges whose guards are enabled?

quotes: flow inputs delivered along every edge from them — a flow input or output endpoint is the node_id empty string (A05 rule 2) —,

An edge whose source is a flow input (the node_id empty string) is decided from the start, since every flow input is delivered when the run starts: without a guard it is enabled, and a guarded one is decided as above from the flow input its guard_port names.
enabled when that value's canonical JSON text equals guard_value and disabled otherwise;
judgement.why: One passage requires delivery along every flow-input edge, while the guard rules allow a flow-input edge to be disabled.

topics.topic: Whether execute_function_element must reuse ports read by advance_run or may reread them through read_implementation, and which contract must change
questions: Must advance_run stop requiring the function-node ports to be read once per advance and passed only through NodePorts, or must execute_function_element's contract or requirements change so it can reuse those already-read ports instead of obtaining the contract version and its ports again through read_implementation?
Must execute_function_element reuse the ports read once by advance_run, which its contract cannot receive, or may it read and use the contract version and its ports again through read_implementation?

quotes: The ports a node's inputs and outputs are checked against MUST come from what the node names: a function node's from read_contract_version of its pinned implementation's contract version, an operation node's from read_binding of its binding_id; they are read once per advance and passed to plan_run as one NodePorts per flow node in node_id order.

execute_function_element: [ORCHESTRATION] MUST read the pinned implementation of the node with read_implementation, read every input's bytes with read_value_bytes into PortPayloads by port, take started_at from kernel_now, and call execute_function with the code, the payloads, the contract version's input and output ports and its resource_bounds; it writes no record and returns the outcome for its caller to write.
judgement.why: The first passage requires function ports to be read once per advance through read_contract_version, while the second requires execute_function_element to obtain and use the contract version and its ports through read_implementation.

topics.topic: How recover_running_runs should reconcile RunPlan InputSource outputs with RecordRunProgressChange output types
questions: Must recover_running_runs convert each RunPlan InputSource with record_flow_output before constructing RecordRunProgressChange, or must RunPlan.outputs or RecordRunProgressChange.outputs change type?

quotes: A run plan_run derives as still waiting is not advanced: when its stored status or waiting points differ from what plan_run derives, they are rewritten in one RecordRunProgressChange with no execution, plan_run's status, waiting points and outputs, and no element is reached — an approved element whose in-flight attempt recovery turned unknown waits with reason outcome_unknown and its run rests pending; a run whose stored state already matches is not written.

RecordRunProgressChange fields (exact, no others exist): change: Literal['record_run_progress'], run_id: str, executions: tuple[NodeExecutionDraft, ...], stored_values: tuple[StoredValue, ...], spooled_files: tuple[SpooledFile, ...], status: RunStatus, outputs: tuple[PortRef, ...], waiting: tuple[WaitingPoint, ...], ended_at: KernelInstant | None

RunPlan fields (exact, no others exist): conclusions: tuple[ElementState, ...], edges: tuple[EdgeState, ...], derived: tuple[NodeExecutionDraft, ...], next_node: ReadyNode | None, waiting: tuple[WaitingPoint, ...], outputs: tuple[InputSource, ...], missing_outputs: tuple[MissingOutput, ...], status: RunStatus
judgement.why: The requirement directs recover_running_runs to put RunPlan.outputs into RecordRunProgressChange.outputs, but those fields respectively require InputSource and PortRef tuples.
